title: First called Christians (Acts 11)
hook: a famous sentence with a blank in it: called Christians, by whom?
tomorrow: how does a man sleep the night before his trial?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Peter in a room full of Gentiles, discovering that God plays no favorites. The line: no respecter of persons.

Nicknames are rarely chosen. A teammate says one once, it sticks, and years later it's written on a birthday cake. Acts has a sentence like that, and it's famous: "And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch." Now read it again, slowly. Called by whom? The sentence has no one doing the calling. Somebody handed the believers the name, and Acts leaves the somebody blank. So where did it come from, and what was in it?
screen: `NICKNAMES ARE RARELY CHOSEN.` → `CALLED CHRISTIANS FIRST IN ANTIOCH.` → `CALLED BY WHOM?`

segments.voice: Start with who was there. After Stephen's death, believers scatter, and Acts says they share the word with Jews only. Then some men of Cyprus and Cyrene reach Antioch and start talking to Greeks as well, "And the hand of the Lord was with them." A new, mixed community starts meeting in a big city. Jerusalem sends Barnabas to look. When he "had seen the grace of God, was glad." He goes to Tarsus to find Saul and brings him back, and for a whole year the two of them teach there. Then the name. Here's the honest answer to the puzzle: the text doesn't say who coined it, and anyone who tells you for certain is reading outside Acts. What the text does give is the name's core. Christian is built on Christ, and a chapter earlier Peter had said what that title meant to them: "God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power." Some readers hear an even smaller name inside it: little christs, people carrying his name down a city street where the neighbors can see whether it fits. And the very next scene shows what the named people did. A prophet named Agabus warns of a famine, so the disciples, "every man according to his ability," send relief to the believers in Judaea. The name arrives, and the first thing they do with it is take up a collection.
screen: `A MIXED CHURCH IN ANTIOCH.` · `THE TEXT DOESN'T SAY WHO.` · `A NAME BUILT ON CHRIST.` · `FIRST THING THEY DID: A COLLECTION.` · then, large: `LITTLE CHRISTS.`

segments.voice: Say your own name out loud, once, slowly. Then say one word you'd hope people hear in it when you're not in the room: kind, honest, steady. Sit with the space between the two without judging it, and say your name once more at the end.
Christian. A name the disciples were given in Antioch, built on Christ, the anointed one.
The line for today: little christs, a name they were handed and had to grow into. Day done.

fork.setup: kids at school start calling your friend group 'the church kids,' and it sticks. what does Antioch suggest?

what it means: a name the disciples were given in Antioch, by people Acts never names.
what a scholar hears: the verb in Acts 11:26 has no named subject. the word comes back in Acts 26:28 and 1 Peter 4:16.

options: Acts says they were first called Christians in Antioch, but never says who called them.
Paul named them himself in Antioch, after teaching there with Barnabas a whole year.
Jesus gave the name to his disciples just before he ascended into heaven.
chat.meaning: And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch: the sentence never names who did the calling. The name was given, not chosen.

Antioch.meaning: a big city where a mixed church of Jews and Greeks met

Agabus.meaning: a prophet who warned of a famine
